persona.role: Freelance brand and visual identity designer
current_work: Social media campaign assets for an existing client
priorities: Complete the new brand identity brief
Finish the Northstar Coffee portfolio case study

circumstances: The client approved the revised identity direction. Final logo variants, typography details, color specifications, and organized source files were prepared and the completed handoff package was sent. This closes the active identity deliverable unless further client changes arrive.
One requested campaign format was adapted, exported, uploaded, and sent to the existing client for confirmation.

The unfinished Northstar Coffee case study received a substantial narrative and visual refinement block, including a clearer problem/process opening and tighter final-result presentation, but it was not published.
Behance and YouTube may have supported professional reference or learning, but the raw events do not establish their exact usefulness or whether they were necessary.
A short lettering exercise occurred separately from client and portfolio work.

activities.title: New food-business identity — design work
activities.summary: Read client response approving the revised identity direction and asking for final logo exports, color values, and font details. Updated the project checklist with the final handoff items and export requirements. Reviewed the approved identity system and checked logo variants, spacing, and color applications before export. Prepared primary and secondary logo lockups and cleaned vector paths for final delivery.

activities.title: Social campaign — design work
activities.summary: Answered a small question from the existing social campaign client about the correct asset format. Reviewed the social campaign master file and identified the remaining requested format. Adapted the existing campaign design into the requested square format. Adjusted image crop, text hierarchy, and spacing for the social campaign variant.

activities.title: Northstar portfolio case study — design work
activities.summary: Opened the Northstar Coffee portfolio case study and reviewed the current narrative and image sequence. Reworked the case-study opening section to explain the design problem, constraints, and identity direction. Added final Northstar identity applications and selected a smaller set of project visuals for the case study. Drafted concise project notes describing the brief, process, and final outcome for the portfolio case study.

activities.title: Reference browsing and video — purpose not observable
activities.summary: Browsed several branding case studies while considering presentation structure; direct usefulness to the Northstar case study is uncertain.

activities.title: Northstar portfolio case study — design work
activities.summary: Returned to the Northstar case study and adjusted the visual rhythm between the process and final-result sections.

activities.title: Personal lettering practice — design work
activities.summary: Spent a short block experimenting with a personal lettering treatment unrelated to client deliverables.

activities.title: Reference browsing and video — purpose not observable
activities.summary: Watched a typography workflow video; whether it contributed to current work is not established.

activities.title: Northstar portfolio case study — files and delivery
activities.summary: Saved and organized the latest Northstar portfolio draft; the case study is still not published.

key_observations: The client approval created a concrete closure point for the new identity rather than another open-ended revision cycle.
Finalization work was directly tied to the approved identity and produced a complete handoff package.
The social campaign request was handled in a bounded production block without consuming the main identity handoff period.
The Northstar portfolio received a sustained block focused on both storytelling and visual curation, making more progress than in several recent days.
Behance and YouTube activity may have been useful references or learning, but the evidence does not justify labeling either as distraction or necessary work.
The offline period leaves some activity unobserved.
